threads.thread_goal: Align on scope, roles, and timeline for the budgeting process rollout.

messages.text: Team, welcome to the official channel for the new Budgeting and Forecasting Process Rollout. The main goal is to create a unified, compliant, and transparent process for the whole company. Please review the project brief and let's confirm our roles and the high-level timeline.

Thanks for kicking this off. I've read the brief. My understanding is I'll be handling the initial discovery and documentation, starting with mapping the current state as per T1, and then later compiling the final process doc A3. I can start drafting a survey for the department heads this afternoon.
Looks good. The objective is clear. The 21-day deadline seems tight but achievable if we stay on track. What's our first major milestone date?
Ok, I see my part is designing the templates. Does the scope include creating templates for capex requests too, or just operational budgets?
Good question. For this first cycle, let's focus strictly on operational budgets to keep it manageable. We can add capex in a future iteration. Let's lock that in as part of the scope.
Understood. I will be responsible for the data reconciliation.
First milestone is to have the draft templates and the current state analysis done by the end of next week. That gives us time for review and piloting before the next planning cycle.

That makes sense. Limiting the scope to operational budgets will help us meet the deadline. I've also noted that T6, defining the governance workflow, will be critical. We should probably schedule a short meeting with the Finance Director next week to get their input early.
Ok, operational budgets only. Thanks for clarifying.
End of next week for drafts works for me. I'll block some time to support the review.

Good point, I'll set up that meeting. So, to summarize and confirm:
1. Scope is a unified process for operational budgeting and forecasting, with key deliverables as listed in the brief. (D1)
2. Our timeline is 21 days, with the first major milestone being draft templates and current state analysis by end of next week. (D2)
Does everyone agree?
Confirmed.
Agreed.
Yes, confirmed.
Agree.
Great. We are aligned. Next steps are clear.
Survey for T1 is drafted. I'll send it out tomorrow morning.
When should I start looking at the historical data?
You can start this week. We'll need that baseline ready for when the templates are drafted.

threads.thread_goal: Design and finalize the standard budget and cash-flow templates.

messages.text: Hi team, here is the first draft of the Standard Budget Template (A1). Please let me know your thoughts. I tried to map it to the main accounts.

Thanks for sharing. I've left some comments in the sheet. The structure is a good start, but we need more granularity on the expense side to align with the detailed chart of accounts, especially for SG&A costs. Otherwise, budget vs. actual analysis will be difficult. Also, could we add a small section for headcount planning? It's a key driver for many departments.

Thanks. While everyone reviews A1, I've started outlining the 12-Month Rolling Cash-Flow Forecast Model (A2) as part of T3. The main challenge will be standardizing our assumptions. I've created a separate tab in the model for key inputs like DSO, DPO, and inventory days. We need to agree on a baseline for these. I've put some initial thoughts in A7.
Agree with the comments on A1. We should also make sure the template is easy for non-finance managers to use. Maybe we can lock the formula cells and add some instructions at the top.
Ok, I see the comments. I can add more detail for SG&A. For the headcount, should I just add a line for salaries or a full section with roles and monthly costs?
Let's go with a simple table: Role, Headcount (FTE), and Total Monthly Salary Cost. That should be enough for this purpose and keeps the template from getting too complex.

Regarding the cash-flow assumptions in A7, I suggest we use a 3-month historical average for DSO and DPO as our baseline. For seasonality, we can apply a percentage uplift based on last year's sales data. We need to document these clearly.
Ok, I will add that table and the other changes. I will also lock the cells as suggested.
Using a 3-month average for payment terms sounds reasonable. It reflects recent performance. I'm good with that approach.

Perfect. Let's formalize these decisions then.
1. The budget template (A1) structure is approved with the addition of detailed SG&A lines, a simple headcount section, and locked formula cells. (D3)
2. For the cash-flow model (A2), we'll use a 3-month historical average for DSO/DPO and last year's data for seasonality as our baseline assumptions. (D4)
@98074 please share the updated A1 when ready.
Will do. I should have the new version by tomorrow morning.
Sounds good. This gives us a solid foundation for the pilot.

threads.thread_goal: Resolve data quality issues and confirm the baseline dataset.

messages.text: Update on T4: I've been looking at the historical data for the last 24 months. There are some inconsistencies in how expenses were categorized, especially in Q3 of last year.
Thanks for the update. Can you be more specific? Which expense accounts are affected? Is it a mapping issue or are there unreconciled transactions?
It's mostly marketing and travel expenses. Some entries seem to be in the wrong sub-account. I think we changed the chart of accounts around that time.
We could go back and reclassify everything from that period. It would take some time but the data would be clean.

Given our timeline, reclassifying 24 months of data isn't feasible. The goal here is to get a reasonable baseline for the first forecast and the BvA reports (A5), not to conduct a full historical audit.

I agree. The 'cost of quality' is too high here. What if we limit our baseline to the last 12 months? The data is more recent and should be more consistent. We can add a note about the historical data issues for context.
Using the last 12 months makes sense. It's recent enough to be relevant for forecasting and avoids the problematic period. I support that approach.
So I should only focus on reconciling the last 12 months?

Yes, exactly. Let's make a decision on this so we can move forward. We will use the last 12 months of reconciled data from the main P&L ledgers as the official baseline for this project. (D5) @44926 please focus on getting that dataset cleaned and exported by the end of the week.
Ok, I will do that.
Decision captured. This unblocks the creation of the pilot BvA report (A5).
Understood.

threads.thread_goal: Plan and execute the pilot with one business unit and capture feedback.

messages.text: Team, now that the templates are stable and the baseline data is ready, it's time to plan the pilot (T9). I propose we use the Marketing department. They have a fairly complex budget and their manager is engaged and open to providing feedback. I suggest we run it next week, from Monday to Wednesday. Thoughts?
Marketing is a great choice. If the process works for them, it will likely work for everyone else. The timeline for next week is good, it's before they get busy with end-of-month campaigns.

I agree with Marketing as the pilot unit. I've gone ahead and set up a document for capturing feedback (A8). I'll share it with the Marketing manager and schedule a short debrief session for next Thursday to discuss their experience with the budget template (A1) and the process.
Sounds good. I will be available to support them if they have questions about the template.
Excellent initiative, thanks. So we're agreed on the pilot unit and schedule. (D6) I'll coordinate with the Marketing manager to kick things off on Monday.

Quick update: The pilot with Marketing is complete. Overall, the feedback was very positive. They found the new budget template (A1) much clearer than the old one. The main feedback points are logged in A8.

I've reviewed the log (A8). The key suggestion is to add a dedicated field for 'Campaign Code' next to major marketing expenses. This would help them track budget vs. actuals for specific initiatives. It seems like a simple change to A1 that would add a lot of value for them.
That's great news. Did they have any comments on the cash-flow forecast (A2) or the BvA report (A5)?
They found the BvA report (A5) very insightful, especially the variance commentary. No specific feedback on the cash-flow model (A2) as that's more of an internal finance tool.
So we need to add another column to the template? Will this mess up the formulas for the totals?
It shouldn't be a problem. It would be a text field, so it won't affect the sum ranges. We can add it to the left of the cost columns. It's a minor structural change.
I agree, it's a valuable and low-effort change. Let's approve this modification based on the pilot feedback. (D7) @98074 can you please update the final version of A1 with this 'Campaign Code' field?
Ok, I will add the column.

threads.thread_goal: Finalize controls, documentation, and training before full rollout.

messages.text: Hi all, as we approach the rollout, I've uploaded the draft of the final process documentation (A3) and the user guide (A6) for review. These documents cover the end-to-end process (T10) and instructions for the templates. Please provide any feedback by tomorrow EOD.

This is excellent, thanks for putting it together so quickly. I've done a quick pass and it looks comprehensive. I just added a note about the quarterly review of forecast assumptions, which links to T12.
The documents look great. Clear and easy to follow. This will be very helpful for the business unit managers.

I am reviewing the documents now. In parallel, I am working on the internal control checklist (A4) for T7. I have a question about the tax compliance part (T11). Is our standard depreciation schedule sufficient or do I need to reference specific tax codes?

For the checklist (A4), it's best to be explicit. I'd suggest adding a line item that says 'Depreciation assumptions for key asset classes reviewed against current tax legislation'. This ensures the check is performed without getting bogged down in specific codes in the checklist itself. The detailed support can be kept in the working papers.
Ok, that makes sense. I will add that line. Thank you.
That's the right approach. The checklist should verify the control is performed, not replicate the entire procedure. Once A4 is finalized, we'll have all the key components ready for go-live.
I've incorporated the feedback on A3 and A6. They are now final. @98074 let us know when A4 is ready for a final look.
The checklist A4 is ready for review now.

Looks good. I've reviewed it and it covers all the necessary controls. With that, I believe we are ready to sign off on all documentation and controls. I propose we formally approve the full package: internal controls (A4), final documentation (A3), and the training plan outlined in the user guide (A6). (D8) Any objections?
Approved. I'll schedule the training sessions for next week.
No objections. Approved.
Approved.
Great work, everyone. We are officially ready for rollout. This has been a fantastic team effort.
